skin.setting: a whaling station on a sub-antarctic island, 1912
skin.title: Blood on the Ice
skin.place: Grytviken Whaling Station, South Georgia Island
skin.styleGuide: Gloomy sub-antarctic polar gothic with wood and corrugated iron buildings, steam, sea spray, and muted cold lighting.

rooms.name: the flensing hall
rooms.description: A cavernous timber hall with blood-soaked floorboards where whale carcasses are stripped.

rooms.name: the boiler room
rooms.description: A stifling room dominated by heavy iron cookers venting hissing steam into the frost.

rooms.name: the slipway
rooms.description: An exposed timber ramp sloping into the churning, icy waters of the bay.

rooms.name: the oil store
rooms.description: A cold, low-ceilinged vault stacked high with filled whale-oil casks.

rooms.name: the cooperage
rooms.description: A workshop littered with iron hoops, wooden staves, and dried cedar shavings.

rooms.name: the bone mill
rooms.description: A loud grinding chamber where dried whale bone is crushed into powder.

people.name: Einar Lindqvist
people.bio: A veteran Norwegian whaler known for his icy nerve and dead aim. He has clashed bitterly over pay cuts enforced this winter season.
people.voice: Speaks with a gravelly, clipped tone, indifferent to pleasantries.
people.motive: Grønn withheld his share of the season's lucrative whale oil bonus.
people.portrait: A weathered man in his late forties with a thick grey beard, hollow cheeks, wearing a grease-stained wool sweater and heavy canvas trousers, standing erect.

people.name: Henrik Vang
people.bio: The company bureaucrat tasked with keeping the remote station profitable. His logbooks have recently drawn intense scrutiny from the shipping line.
people.voice: Dry, precise, and calculating, speaking as if dictating a ledger entry.
people.motive: Grønn discovered evidence that Vang was embezzling cargo manifests.
people.portrait: A thin, bespectacled man in his late thirties with slicked dark hair, wearing a stiff-collared woollen vest and buttoned tweed coat.

people.name: Torvald Næss
people.bio: A mechanic who keeps the station boilers and steam winches running under brutal conditions. He frequently argued with the captain over unsafe operating pressures.
people.voice: Gruff, loud, and raspy from inhaling coal smoke and steam.
people.motive: Grønn blamed him for an engine failure and threatened to ruin his career.
people.portrait: A broad-shouldered, muscular man with soot-smudged skin, unkempt brown hair, dressed in a heavy flannel tunic and oilskin trousers.

people.name: Aksel Berg
people.bio: A rugged deckhand who wields flensing knives with surgical precision. He had recently received notice of his dismissal without passage home.
people.voice: Low, sullen, and guarded, reluctant to speak to authority.
people.motive: Grønn fired him and planned to maroon him on the island through the winter.
people.portrait: A burly young man with a rugged jaw, dark stubble, and tangled hair, wearing an unbuttoned heavy mackinaw coat over a faded wool shirt.

people.name: Magnus Dahl
people.bio: A nervous man responsible for rations, supplies, and winter provisions. He has lived in dread of the harsh winter freeze and dwindling rations.
people.voice: Soft, hesitant, and constantly clearing his throat before answering.
people.motive: Grønn caught him hoarding emergency provisions and threatened criminal charges.
people.portrait: A pale, gaunt man with nervous blue eyes, receding fair hair, wearing a patched knit cardigan and stained woollen apron.

people.name: Olaf Grønn
people.bio: The tyrannical master of the whaling station and its ships. His ruthless discipline earned him universal hatred among the crew.
people.voice: A booming, imperious growl that brooked no contradiction.
people.portrait: A stout, imposing man with an iron-grey spade beard, stern cold eyes, wearing a dark double-breasted naval greatcoat.

skin.briefing: On a frozen sub-antarctic evening, Captain Olaf Grønn was found dead among the barrels in the oil store at Grytviken Whaling Station. A blizzard has sealed the station off from the rest of the island, meaning the killer remains among the few men stationed within the facility. You must retrace the movements of the crew across the station's buildings between five o'clock and ten o'clock to uncover the truth.
skin.scene: A bleak sub-antarctic whaling station under snow, featuring rustic corrugated iron sheds, weathered wooden jetties, and smoking boiler chimneys against icy mountains.
skin.summingUp:
Listen to the sea spray lashing the corrugated iron and the steam rattling in the pipes. In this freezing gloom, Olaf Grønn met his end in the oil store, struck down because he withheld the share of the season's lucrative whale oil bonus. We only needed to establish the hour and the presence in that shed to see the truth clearly.

First, the murder was not at five o'clock or ten o'clock, because Card 3 narrows down when the murder happened. The murder was not at six o'clock, because Card 6 puts Olaf Grønn in company, and so still alive. Furthermore, the murder was not at eight o'clock or nine o'clock, because Card 10 narrows down when the murder happened. That leaves precisely seven o'clock.

We know that the killer and Olaf Grønn were both in the oil store when it happened. Because of this, Aksel Berg and Magnus Dahl are in the clear. Henrik Vang is in the clear, because the killer and Olaf Grønn were both in the oil store when it happened. Torvald Næss is in the clear as well, because the killer and Olaf Grønn were both in the oil store when it happened. By elimination across the station, only one person remains: Einar Lindqvist.
